title: Semantic alias map and theme choreography for console consistency review
creator: Asha Raman
description: Review and unify a semantic alias layer and a small choreography pattern set for console theming. Goal is to provide a human-friendly mapping (alias map) from product intent to token values, a set of deterministic component state transitions (choreography) and a minimal set of motion/spacing rhythms so engineering can implement a single coherent theme across dashboards, rollout controls, and cost views without proliferating visual exceptions. This ticket covers audit findings, proposed alias schema, prototype updates in Figma, and a migration plan for existing components.
scope: Audit all frequently used surface and interaction states for dashboard cards, rollout rails, metric chips, cost breakdown tables, and toast/inline alerts. Produce alias map, choreographed state diagrams, and Figma component updates for: primary/secondary accents, emphasis surfaces, interactive focus rings, disabled/low-opacity states, hover elevation, and compact/comfortable density modes.
acceptance_criteria: A1: A published semantic alias map (CSV + human-readable doc) that covers at least 85% of tokens used on main console surfaces
A2: Figma library updated with renamed semantic components and a token inspector prototype demonstrating alias switching between light/dark/dim themes
A3: Choreography patterns documented for focus, hover, pressed, and transitional states of rollout controls and metric cards with measurable motion timings
A4: Accessibility checks: contrast ratios >= 4.5:1 for body text on all primary surfaces and WCAG keyboard focus visible across updated components
A5: Migration plan with a timeline and list of deprecated tokens plus a compatibility shim for at least 6 months
design_notes: Decision: Use semantic aliases (e.g., 'surface-muted', 'accent-critical', 'focus-ring') rather than exposing raw ramp tokens to product teams.
Trade-off: Aliases reduce cognitive load but require an initial mapping effort and extra runtime translation layer; agreed to accept short-term engineering cost for long-term maintainability.
Edge cases: Legacy dashboards use hard-coded hex values in one-off widgets; propose temporary compatibility CSS vars and a migration ticket for each widget owner.
Motion rhythm: Base easing is 120ms ease-out for micro interactions, 240ms for card transitions. Keep motion minimal on high-density dashboards to avoid perceived latency.
Internationalization: Ensure alias naming avoids culture-specific metaphors; prefer intent-driven names like 'emphasis-strong' instead of color metaphors.
Density modes: Provide 'compact' and 'comfortable' component variants with consistent vertical rhythm multiples (4px increments).
Fallback: For on-prem customers who cannot upgrade immediately, include a 'legacy' alias mapping file in the release bundle.
review_comments: Daniel Chu (Eng): 'Alias layer looks good. Need a small API doc showing runtime variable names and how to toggle alias sets per-tenant.'

Ethan Park (Accessibility): 'Observed low contrast on compact metric chip in dark-mode; recommend adjusting emphasis-strong or using a stronger background blend.'
Marina Lopez (Design): 'Approve prototype pending two fixes: add explicit focus outline state and add deprecation notice to component docs.'
Follow-up: Add ENG-73421 for runtime alias toggle API and DES-182510 for deprecation communications plan.
decisions: Adopt semantic alias layer as canonical surface naming convention
Keep the current token ramp (raw values) as a source-of-truth but discourage direct reference in new components
Ship alias inspector in Figma so PMs and SEs can preview theme permutations
tradeoffs: Short-term: Increased onboarding for engineers to learn alias mapping vs long-term: faster product changes and safer A/Bing of visual changes
Defer: Deep color-blindness palettes will be considered in a follow-up once alias layer stabilized
